chunks: Allah may be bad to Maṣqalah!
He acted like the noble but fled away like a slave!
Before his admirer could speak (about him) he silenced him and before his eulogist could testify to his good deeds he closed his mouth.
If he had stayed behind we would have taken from him what he could easily pay and waited for the balance till his money increased.

key_terms.مَصْقَلَة: Maṣqalah, a companion of Imam Ali who defected to Syria
key_terms.مَيْسُور: What is easily accessible or payable

ai.seo_question: Who is Maṣqalah and what does this passage say about his character and defection?
ai.summary: This passage from Nahj al-Balagha’s letter to Maṣqalah al-Khuzāʿī employs sharp rhetorical contrast to expose his hypocrisy, juxtaposing his claim to noble status with his cowardly flight like a slave. The phrase 'what praised him did not speak until he silenced him' alludes to his eloquence being nullified by the truth of his actions, while the final clause references the financial tribute (khums or tribute) he would have paid had he stayed loyal. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of Maṣqalah as a key figure in the early Umayyad consolidation of power, whose defection symbolized the shift from the caliphate of justice to that of dynastic rule.
